parts.visual:
A startup pays $0 in advertising. User A downloads the app. In order to use the app properly, User A must invite User B and User C. Now the startup has 3 users. User B and User C invite two more people each. The startup now has 7 users. This mathematical explosion is called a Viral Loop.

The Viral Coefficient (K-Factor):
1. The K-Factor: The exact number of new users that every existing user successfully recruits. If K is 1.2, every 10 users invite 12 new users. The company will grow infinitely with zero marketing budget.
2. Built-in Virality vs. Artificial Virality: True virality happens when the product is literally useless unless you invite a friend (like WhatsApp). Artificial virality is offering someone $10 to invite a friend (like Uber or PayPal).
parts.audio: Virality is not 'making a funny video on TikTok.' In Silicon Valley, virality is a strict mathematical formula engineered directly into the software's core mechanics. You must force your users to become your unpaid sales team.

questions.question: What happens if a startup's 'K-Factor' is 0.8?
options: The viral loop will eventually die out. A K-Factor of 0.8 means every 10 users only invite 8 new users. The next generation is smaller than the last. To achieve infinite exponential growth, the K-Factor must be strictly greater than 1.0.
questions.correct_answer: The viral loop will eventually die out. A K-Factor of 0.8 means every 10 users only invite 8 new users. The next generation is smaller than the last. To achieve infinite exponential growth, the K-Factor must be strictly greater than 1.0.
questions.explanation: If K < 1, the fire eventually burns out.

questions.question: Listen to the growth hacker explaining Dropbox's early strategy. What was their famous referral engine?
questions.tts_text: We were spending $300 on Google Ads to get a customer who only paid us $99. We were dying. So, we stopped buying ads. Instead, we gave users 500 megabytes of free storage space for every friend they successfully invited. We gamified the storage.
options: The Double-Sided Incentive. Dropbox rewarded BOTH the person sending the invite (more space) and the person accepting the invite (more space). This artificial virality exploded their growth from 100,000 to 4 million users in 15 months.
questions.correct_answer: The Double-Sided Incentive. Dropbox rewarded BOTH the person sending the invite (more space) and the person accepting the invite (more space). This artificial virality exploded their growth from 100,000 to 4 million users in 15 months.
questions.explanation: A bribe only works if both sides win.

questions.question: Why did Hotmail grow so incredibly fast in 1996 without a marketing budget?
options: The 'Inherent Virality' signature. At the bottom of every single email sent by a Hotmail user, the company automatically attached a line of text: 'Get your free email at Hotmail'. Every time a user used the product, they were advertising it to a non-user.
questions.correct_answer: The 'Inherent Virality' signature. At the bottom of every single email sent by a Hotmail user, the company automatically attached a line of text: 'Get your free email at Hotmail'. Every time a user used the product, they were advertising it to a non-user.
questions.explanation: The product itself is the billboard.

questions.question: What is the danger of relying purely on a viral loop for growth?
options: Viral Degradation. The early adopters invite their friends quickly, but eventually, everyone in the target market has already seen the invite. The K-Factor naturally drops over time, meaning the startup must eventually build traditional sales channels.
questions.correct_answer: Viral Degradation. The early adopters invite their friends quickly, but eventually, everyone in the target market has already seen the invite. The K-Factor naturally drops over time, meaning the startup must eventually build traditional sales channels.
questions.explanation: You eventually run out of fresh humans.
